MEASURED (chromium, master.html?v=paper&state=publish, 1440x960): the page's own fixture accessors return today 2026-07-16, publication.publishedAt 2026-07-15T18:30:00.000Z (state 'published'), primaryDate 2026-10-03, toDay() = 79, days(publishedAt, wedding) = 80, days(publishedAt, today) = 1. Painted: .b-ogNum '79' at 64px/400 (x221 y431) - the single largest type on the screen - .b-ogDate 'days away when this was sent' at 15px directly beneath it, and .b-pressTitle 'Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.' at 48px/600 (x562 y356), the second largest. Identical in ?v=ink. The card's own aria-label is 'Mara & Finn, 79 days away when this was sent. Wedding day, Saturday 3 October 2026'. So the caption dates the figure to a send the headline beside it dates to 15 July, when the distance was 80. The finding's every figure reproduces exactly. THE FROZEN-ASSET DEFENCE FAILS. card() (render-b.js:1831) reads F.toDay() - days(TODAY, wedding) - and touches F.publication nowhere; the publish screen labels the plate 'What lands in the message' and the comment at 1917 calls it 'a fixed asset that lands in somebody else's chat client', but the figure inside it is not fixed to the send, it tracks today. Today is NOT the send date on this screen: the fixture puts them one day apart on purpose, precisely so pressHead's since>=1 branch (the round-11 possession fix) can render. The qualifier's own comment - 'the card has to be true a month later ... the sentence under it says when it was true' - is the strongest evidence FOR the finding: it declares the figure to be the send-day distance, and the code measures it from today. NOT SETTLED. panel/SETTLED.md carries 'publish-contradicts-its-own-headline' (brand, refuted round 8), but that objection was tone - the strap 'Ready to send. The link is below.' against the headline - and its refutation LEANS ON this card's qualifier as the honest thing on the screen, quoting round 7's 'it contradicts the card beside it, which already says when this was sent'. Nobody ever measured the number under the qualifier. 'draft-branch-restored-before-it-is-used' (round 9) drove the draft press screen and called what it saw a 'draft card' - the card has no draft branch at all. New mechanism, new evidence. WORSE THAN FILED, AND NO ARITHMETIC REQUIRED. Driving state=owner-draft and pressing Publish lands on the publish screen with publication draft: headline 'Send it to Mara & Finn.' beside a card reading '79' / 'days away when this was sent'. Nothing has been sent and the card says it was. After pressing Copy the link the headline becomes 'Mara & Finn can open this as soon as you send it.' and the caption still says 'when this was sent'. That contradiction is plain English on one screen - a reader does not have to count 80 days from 15 July to 3 October to see it. GATE. interaction-check.mjs:3667-3679 opens state=unfurl and asserts only /when this was sent|the day/ against the aria-label; it never checks the figure, and no assertion anywhere pins the card to 79 (the only '79' hits in the gate are rgb(79,70,229)). This is the round's own 'a passing assertion that proves nothing' class. FIX IS SOUND: measuring from publishedAt gives 80, which agrees with 'since 15 July', and the phone/desk 96px count stays 79 - the drift the qualifier exists to explain. In scope: no colour, no weight, no restructure; one accessor, one string.

Gate both on the SAME test pressHead already uses. Lift the send day into one accessor beside pressHead - `function sentDay() { var p = F.publication.publishedAt; return p && F.days(p, F.today) >= 1 ? String(p).slice(0, 10) : null; }` - then in card() `var sent = sentDay(); var said = F.countdown(F.days(sent || F.today, F.project.primaryDate.date));` and caption `said.unit + (sent ? " away when this was sent" : " away")`, with figureSaid built from the same two variables. All three publication branches then agree on one screen: handed over ('80 days away when this was sent' / 'have had this since 15 July.'), just copied ('79 days away' / 'can open this as soon as you send it.'), and draft ('79 days away' / 'Send it to Mara & Finn.'). state=unfurl keeps the qualifier, so interaction-check.mjs:3676 still passes. While there, make that gate assertion prove something: assert the numeral in the aria-label equals days(publishedAt, primaryDate), not merely that the words are present.
